# nish/net/prefork

Run a server on every core: a supervisor process that starts one worker process per core, restarts one that dies, and stops them all on SIGTERM or SIGINT (`docs/wp42-multicore-server.md` §2.3).

```ts
import {
  PREFORK_CHANNELS_FLAG,
  PREFORK_LISTENER_FLAG,
  PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED,
  PREFORK_STOPPED,
  PREFORK_WORKERS_EXITED,
  PREFORK_WORKER_FLAG,
  PreforkConfig,
  preforkArgs,
  preforkIndex,
  preforkListener,
  preforkServiceChannel,
  preforkServiceChannelOf,
  preforkSupervise,
  preforkSupervisorChannel,
  preforkWith,
  preforkWorkerCount,
  preforkWorkers,
} from "nish/net/prefork";
```

```ts
import { tcpListenFlags } from "nish:net";
import { preforkWorkers } from "nish/net/prefork";

export const main = (): number => {
  const worker: i32 = preforkWorkers(process.argv);
  if (worker < 0) { return worker === -1 ? 0 : 1; } // the supervisor, done
  const listener = tcpListenFlags("0.0.0.0", 8080, 1024, 1); // SO_REUSEPORT
  // ... the single-threaded readiness loop, unchanged ...
};
```

<scalar-detail title="One program, two roles">

`preforkWorkers(process.argv)` answers in two kinds of
process. In a worker it answers the worker's index, `0` to `N - 1`, at once,
and the program goes on to bind its listener and serve. In the process the
user started it supervises, and answers only once every worker has exited:
`-1` after a shutdown, `-2` when the workers could not be started or the
supervisor could not listen for signals. Each worker binds its own listener
with `tcpListenFlags`' flag 1 (`SO_REUSEPORT`), so on Linux the kernel
spreads new connections across them and no state is shared:
a worker is the single-threaded server it was before, `Arena.used()` flat
per worker.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="How a worker is told">

The supervisor runs the program again with
`--nish-prefork-worker=<index>` appended to its arguments, through `spawn`;
on Linux it runs `/proc/self/exe`, so a program started through `PATH` or a
relative path finds itself. `preforkArgs(process.argv)` answers the
arguments without that flag, for a worker that reads its own; the module
takes `process.argv` from its caller because only a program with a `main`
has one. The environment is inherited whole, and every descriptor the
supervisor holds is close-on-exec, so a worker starts with none of them
but the channel ends below (`docs/security/runtime.md`, RT-17, RT-19).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Channels">

With `supervisorChannels` on, each worker is started with one
end of a fresh `unixSocketPair` (`channelKind`: stream by default, since a
seqpacket pair needs Linux and the supervisor panics on one elsewhere) and
the supervisor keeps the other; `preforkSupervise` hands each readable end to
a callback. With `serviceWorker` set, every other worker gets a pair to that
worker. The ends go through `spawnWithFds`, from descriptor 3 in a fixed
order: the supervisor channel, then a worker's service channel, or in the
service worker its end to each other worker by index, skipping its own. Where
they landed rides in `--nish-prefork-channels=` just before the worker flag,
and `preforkSupervisorChannel`, `preforkServiceChannel` and
`preforkServiceChannelOf` read it back. A pair cannot be handed to a worker
already running, so service channels make the workers one group: when any of
them exits, the supervisor sends the rest SIGTERM (SIGKILL after `graceMs`),
and once none is left, starts them all again on fresh pairs, after the
backoff of the one that exited first. No worker keeps an end whose peer is
gone longer than that. With `restart` off nothing is signalled; a worker sees
its peer's exit as a hang-up.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Listeners and pinning">

With `listenPort` set (0 or above), the
supervisor binds one `SO_REUSEPORT` listener per worker itself, in index
order, keeps them for its whole run and hands listener `k` to every start of
worker `k` after the channel ends; `preforkListener(args)` answers it in the
worker (`--nish-prefork-listener=`, before the channels flag), so a worker
serves that descriptor instead of binding its own. Port 0 binds the first
listener anywhere and the rest to its port. With `pin` on as well, each
listener steers by CPU (`tcpListenFlags`' flag 4): the kernel hands a
connection that arrived on CPU `k` to listener `k`, and a worker that is
restarted takes the same listener, so the order holds across restarts,
which it would not if each worker bound its own. `pin` alone makes each
worker call `setCpuAffinity(k)` before `preforkWith` answers it, so worker
`k` runs on CPU `k` only; a worker the kernel refuses (CPU `k` outside the
process's mask) says so on stderr and runs unpinned. More workers than
`availableParallelism()` is refused with a panic, since a worker past the
last CPU would be pinned nowhere and, steered, handed nothing. Pinning and
steering are Linux's: elsewhere the supervisor says once that the workers
run unpinned, and the listeners are plain `SO_REUSEPORT` ones. Both are off
by default.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="How many">

`NISH_WORKERS` when it is a positive whole number, else
`PreforkConfig.workers` when that is positive, else
`availableParallelism()` on Linux and 1 elsewhere: Darwin shares a
`SO_REUSEPORT` port without spreading connections across it. The count has
no upper bound, so `NISH_WORKERS` is the operator's to set, not a client's.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Restarts">

A worker that exits, by a signal or with any code, is started
again at the same index while the supervisor is not stopping. One that dies
within `quickExitMs` of starting waits before its restart: `backoffMs` the
first time, twice the last wait after that, up to `backoffCapMs`; one that
ran longer starts again at once and clears its wait, so a crash loop costs a
spawn every `backoffCapMs`, not a core. A restart `spawn` refuses waits on
the same backoff and is tried again; only the first start of a worker that
fails ends the supervisor, with `PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Shutdown">

The supervisor listens through `signalFd()`, made before the
first spawn so no signal falls between. On SIGTERM or SIGINT it stops
restarting, sends every worker SIGTERM, reaps them for `graceMs`, sends what
is left SIGKILL and reaps that. A second signal during the grace period sends
SIGKILL at once. The workers get the default dispositions back from `exec`,
so a worker that never asked for `signalFd()` ends on the SIGTERM. A
supervisor that dies any other way (SIGKILL, the OOM killer, or the default
action of SIGHUP or SIGQUIT, which `signalFd()` does not catch) leaves its
workers running, reparented to init.

</scalar-detail>

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

### preforkSupervise

`preforkWith`, calling `onChannel(state, index, fd, events)` in the
supervisor whenever worker `index`'s supervisor channel `fd` is readable or
hung up: `events` is `pollWait`'s, 1 readable and 4 added on a hang-up or
error. The callback reads what is waiting, since an end left readable wakes
the loop again at once, and may write back, but never closes `fd`: the
supervisor closes it after a hang-up, when the worker is reaped and when it
stops, and a restarted worker comes with a new one. Panics, besides, when
`serviceWorker` is not below the worker count or the count is above 64 with
a service worker (63 with `listenPort`), the most `spawnWithFds` hands one
child; when `pin`, on Linux, asks for more workers than
`availableParallelism()`; and, through `preforkInvalid`, on seqpacket
channels off Linux. A listener that cannot bind answers
`PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED` before any worker starts.

```ts
function preforkSupervise<S>(
  args: string[],
  config: PreforkConfig,
  state: S,
  onChannel: (state: S, index: i32, fd: i32, events: i32) => void,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="args" type="string[]" required>

the process's arguments, `process.argv`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="config" type="PreforkConfig" required>

the supervisor's settings, every field checked (a bad one
  panics) in the supervisor and each worker alike; past that check a
  worker reads only `pin`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="state" type="S" required>

the program's own value, passed to every `onChannel` call

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="onChannel" type="(state: S, index: i32, fd: i32, events: i32) =&gt; void" required>

what the supervisor runs when worker `index`'s channel
  `fd` wakes it, with `pollWait`'s `events`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

in a worker, its index at once; in the supervisor, once it is done,
  `PREFORK_STOPPED`, `PREFORK_WORKERS_EXITED` or `PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED`

</scalar-field>

### preforkWith

In a worker, its index. In the supervisor, run the workers until SIGTERM or
SIGINT and answer `PREFORK_STOPPED`; with `restart` off, also until every
worker has exited, answering `PREFORK_WORKERS_EXITED`; or
`PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED` when a worker's
first start failed (those already started are stopped first) or no signal
listener could be made (no worker is started). Panics on a config
`preforkInvalid` names a field of. Supervisor channels are read and
dropped; `preforkSupervise` hands them to the program.

```ts
function preforkWith(
  args: string[],
  config: PreforkConfig,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="args" type="string[]" required>

the process's arguments, `process.argv`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="config" type="PreforkConfig" required>

the supervisor's settings, every field checked (a bad one
  panics) in the supervisor and each worker alike; past that check a
  worker reads only `pin`

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

in a worker, its index at once; in the supervisor, once it is done,
  `PREFORK_STOPPED`, `PREFORK_WORKERS_EXITED` or `PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED`

</scalar-field>

### preforkWorkerCount

How many workers to start: `env` (`NISH_WORKERS`, `null` when unset) when it
is a positive whole number, else `requested` when positive, else the
platform's default.

```ts
function preforkWorkerCount(
  requested: i32,
  env: string | null,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="requested" type="i32" required>

the program's own choice, `PreforkConfig.workers`; 0 or
  less leaves it to the environment or the platform

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="env" type="string | null" required>

the raw `NISH_WORKERS` text, or `null` when it is unset; text
  that is not a positive whole number is ignored

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

how many worker processes the supervisor starts, always 1 or more

</scalar-field>

## Classes

### PreforkConfig

The supervisor's numbers; every one is checked by `preforkWith`.

```ts
class PreforkConfig
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new PreforkConfig()` |  |
| `backoffCapMs: i32` | The longest wait before a restart. |
| `backoffMs: i32` | The first wait before restarting a worker that died young. |
| `channelKind: i32` | What every channel is: `NET_UNIX_STREAM` (1), or `NET_UNIX_SEQPACKET` (2), which keeps each write one message but only Linux has. Stream is the default because it works on Darwin too. |
| `graceMs: i32` | How long the workers get to exit after SIGTERM before SIGKILL. |
| `listenBacklog: i32` | Their backlog. |
| `listenFlags: i32` | Their `tcpListenFlags` beyond `SO_REUSEPORT`, which is always set: 0, or 2 for `TCP_NODELAY`. |
| `listenHost: string` | The address the listeners of `listenPort` bind. |
| `listenPort: i32` | The port the supervisor binds one listener per worker on, 0 for any; -1, the default, leaves each worker to bind its own. |
| `pin: boolean` | Pin worker `k` to CPU `k` (`setCpuAffinity`), and with `listenPort`, steer each connection to the listener of the CPU that received it. Linux only; elsewhere the workers run unpinned. `k` is the CPU number, not the `k`-th allowed CPU: under a mask that skips CPU `k`, worker `k` runs unpinned and a connection received past the listeners falls back to the kernel's hash. |
| `quickExitMs: i32` | A worker that exits within this many milliseconds of starting died young. |
| `restart: boolean` | Start a worker that exited again. Off, a worker that exits stays gone, and the supervisor returns once none is left. |
| `serviceWorker: i32` | The worker every other worker gets a socketpair to; -1 for none. |
| `supervisorChannels: boolean` | Give each worker a socketpair to the supervisor (`preforkSupervise`). |
| `tickMs: i32` | How often, in milliseconds, the supervisor reaps when nothing wakes it. |
| `workers: i32` | Workers to start; 0 takes `NISH_WORKERS` or the platform's default. |

## Constants

<scalar-card title="&quot;--nish-prefork-channels=&quot;" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PREFORK_CHANNELS_FLAG: string`

The argument just before the worker flag when the worker has channels: the
descriptor of its supervisor channel, of its service channel, then in the
service worker of its end to each worker by index, comma-separated, `-1`
for none.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="&quot;--nish-prefork-listener=&quot;" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PREFORK_LISTENER_FLAG: string`

The argument before the channels flag, or before the worker flag when there
is none, when the supervisor holds the listeners: the worker's listener's
descriptor.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PREFORK_SPAWN_FAILED: i32`

What `preforkWith` answers when a worker could not be started, or when the
supervisor could not listen for SIGTERM and so starts none.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PREFORK_STOPPED: i32`

What `preforkWith` answers in the supervisor once its workers are gone.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`PREFORK_WORKERS_EXITED: i32`

What `preforkWith` answers in the supervisor when `restart` is off and every
worker has exited.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="&quot;--nish-prefork-worker=&quot;" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

The argument a worker is started with, its index after the `=`.
